title: What sum should the friend say?
description: An old problem from a ninth century book adds five terms, each one divided by a unit fraction. Each term becomes a whole number by the reciprocal, and the five whole numbers are added.
teaching_notes: One idea: one divided by a unit fraction is the number under the fraction, and the five whole numbers are then added. Watch for students who divide the fractions into one another instead of using the reciprocal.

source: Figure it Out (problems with fractions): the problem from an old Indian book of the 9th century CE, add 1 ÷ 1/6, 1 ÷ 1/10, 1 ÷ 1/13, 1 ÷ 1/9 and 1 ÷ 1/2.
video_script.why: A learner divides one by a unit fraction with the reciprocal, as the fountains did, and adds the results.
video_script.substitution: the book's own five terms, each one divided by a unit fraction
video_script.anchor: the five terms of the old problem, each a one divided by a unit fraction
video_script.fraction_reading: one sixth, one tenth, one thirteenth, one ninth, one half
video_script.design: Five term cards, each turning into a whole number; the whole numbers then join in one sum line.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; five blank cards in a row with a friend asked to add them

marks.cards: five cards appear, each holding one divided by a unit fraction
marks.more: the other three cards light up in turn
marks.ask: a plus sign joins the cards

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book, from an old Indian book of the ninth century.
<bookmark mark='cards'/>A friend is asked to add five terms.
The first two are one divided by one sixth and one divided by one tenth.
<bookmark mark='more'/>The next is one divided by one thirteenth, then one divided by one ninth.
The last is one divided by one half.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What sum should the friend say?

beats.on_screen: the five cards stay on the board; Keeko sits beside them

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: one whole cut into equal pieces, so one divided by a unit fraction counts the pieces

marks.pieces: it is cut into pieces of one sixth
marks.count: the pieces are counted with the reciprocal six

narration: <bookmark mark='whole'/>Take one whole and cut it into pieces of one sixth.
<bookmark mark='pieces'/>Dividing one by one sixth asks how many such pieces fit in the whole.
<bookmark mark='count'/>The reciprocal of one sixth is six, so six pieces fit.

marks.given: the five terms are written in a row

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, five terms, each one divided by a unit fraction.

beats.on_screen: To find: the sum of the five terms

marks.find: the words sum of the five terms are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the sum of the five terms.

marks.six: one divided by one sixth becomes one times six
marks.ten: one divided by one tenth becomes one times ten

narration: <bookmark mark='six'/>Step one, divide by each fraction using its reciprocal, as in the method of your book.
One divided by one sixth is one times six, which is six.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>One divided by one tenth is one times ten, which is ten.

marks.thirteen: one divided by one thirteenth becomes thirteen
marks.nine: one divided by one ninth becomes nine
marks.two: one divided by one half becomes two

narration: <bookmark mark='thirteen'/>Step two, one divided by one thirteenth is thirteen.
<bookmark mark='nine'/>One divided by one ninth is nine.
<bookmark mark='two'/>One divided by one half is two.

marks.add: the five whole numbers are joined with plus signs

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step three, add the five numbers, six plus ten plus thirteen plus nine plus two.

marks.check: the numbers are added again in two groups

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, check by adding in two groups. Six plus nine plus two is seventeen, and ten plus thirteen is twenty three.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The friend should say forty.
Seventeen and twenty three also make forty.
